title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: manage workforce requests from Microsoft 365 Copilot chat
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, request capabilities and security-role controls are supported. The documented role-assignment API matches the printed call, and the gaps about tool-specific licensing, arrival defaults and reviewer-role mapping remain appropriately qualified.

claims.where: front matter: products; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The roadmap identifies Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365) and Dynamics 365 Customer Service as the products.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)", "Dynamics 365 Customer Service"]

claims.claim: WEM integrates with Microsoft 365 Copilot through MCP tools for workforce requests in chat.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 Workforce Engagement Management (WEM) integrates with Microsoft 365 Copilot through Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap target date is July CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "July CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) is the only cloud listed in the roadmap record.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Web as the platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The WEM overview documents three tools for listing requests, opening details and deciding time-off requests.
claims.quote:
list_wem_requests | List workforce requests
get_wem_request_details | Get request details
decide_wem_time_off_request | Approve or reject time-off requests

claims.claim: The request-list tool is named list_wem_requests.
claims.quote: Internal tool name | list_wem_requests

claims.claim: The request-detail tool is named get_wem_request_details.
claims.quote: Internal tool name | get_wem_request_details

claims.claim: The time-off decision tool is named decide_wem_time_off_request.
claims.quote: Internal tool name | decide_wem_time_off_request

claims.claim: Representatives and supervisors do not typically use the MCP tools directly.
claims.quote: Customer service representatives and supervisors don't typically use MCP tools directly. Instead, they interact with Service Agent.

claims.claim: Service Agent determines which tool to use.
claims.quote: Service Agent determines which tool to use, invokes it in the background, and presents the result in the conversation.

claims.claim: Service Agent invokes the selected tool in the background.
claims.quote: Service Agent determines which tool to use, invokes it in the background, and presents the result in the conversation.

claims.claim: Service Agent presents the tool result in the conversation.
claims.quote: Service Agent determines which tool to use, invokes it in the background, and presents the result in the conversation.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The Learn WEM overview names Service Agent as an example conversational experience.
claims.quote: These tools connect a conversational experience, such as Service Agent, with Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Dataverse

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Supervisors can review requests within their authorised planning group.
claims.quote: Supervisors can access records within their authorized planning group, and customer service representatives can access only their own records.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Customer service representatives can list and open only their own workforce requests.
claims.quote: customer service representatives can access only their own records. They can ask for their time-off, shift swap, or shift bid requests, check a request's status, and retrieve details about a specific submission.

claims.claim: Representatives can check request status in the conversation.
claims.quote: They can ask for their time-off, shift swap, or shift bid requests, check a request's status, and retrieve details about a specific submission.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Supervisors with reviewer permission can approve or reject pending time-off requests in chat.
claims.quote: They can filter pending requests, inspect the details and scheduling context for an individual request, and approve or reject time-off requests when they have the required reviewer permission.

claims.claim: Rejecting a time-off request requires a reason.
claims.quote: A rejection reason is required to reject a request. The assistant asks for one if you don't provide it.

claims.claim: The rejection reason is saved as the reviewer note.
claims.quote: A rejection also saves your reason as the reviewer note.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The time-off decision records the reviewer.
claims.quote: The time-off request's status is updated to approved or rejected in Dynamics 365, and you are recorded as the reviewer.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The decision tool changes the request status to approved or rejected in Dynamics 365.
claims.quote: The time-off request's status is updated to approved or rejected in Dynamics 365

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The decision tool does not overwrite another reviewer's existing decision.
claims.quote: It never overwrites a decision another reviewer already made

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Shift-swap and shift-bid requests can be listed and opened but cannot be approved or rejected through these tools.
claims.quote: The current decision capability applies only to time-off requests; shift-swap and shift-bid requests can be listed and reviewed but not approved or rejected through these tools.

claims.claim: The request-list tool is read-only.
claims.quote: No, listing requests doesn't change data. The request list is read-only.

claims.claim: Request lists appear as an interactive list in chat.
claims.quote: The assistant displays an interactive request list as an app-in-chat component.

claims.claim: The request-detail tool is read-only.
claims.quote: No, viewing a request doesn't change data. The request form is a read-only view of the request's details.

claims.claim: Request details appear as an interactive card in chat.
claims.quote: The assistant displays an interactive request card as an app-in-chat component.

claims.claim: The decision tool returns a text confirmation.
claims.quote: The assistant confirms the decision with a text response

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft warns that tool names can change over time.
claims.quote: Tool names, descriptions, parameters, response formats, and available functionality can change over time.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance

claims.quote: Tool names, descriptions, parameters, response formats, and available functionality can change over time.

claims.quote: Tool names, descriptions, parameters, response formats, and available functionality can change over time.

claims.claim: list_wem_requests defaults to team scope.
claims.quote: scope | self or team. Defaults to team—everything you can access.

claims.claim: Without a request-type filter, the list includes every request type the caller can access.
claims.quote: When requestType is omitted, the tool returns all request types (time-off, shift-swap, shift-bid)

claims.claim: Without date filters, the list covers all dates.
claims.quote: When neither from nor to is supplied, the tool applies no date filter (all dates)

claims.claim: Without a status filter, the list covers all statuses.
claims.quote: By default, it shows all requests you can access, of every type, across all dates and statuses.

claims.claim: The default maximum result count is 25.
claims.quote: top | Integer maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 25, capped at 200.

claims.claim: The maximum result count is capped at 200.
claims.quote: top | Integer maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 25, capped at 200.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Team-scope listing relies on Dataverse and WEM security to limit results to readable records.
claims.quote: for the default scope: team, it relies on Dataverse and WEM security to return only rows the caller can read.

claims.claim: Request details can include notes.
claims.quote: Time-off requests—time-off type, whether it's a full day, the start and end of the time off, hours, and notes.

claims.claim: Request details can include review information.
claims.quote: Shift-bid requests—the request's status, dates, and review information. Shift-swap requests—the request's status, dates, and review information.

claims.claim: Time-off request details include the time-off window.
claims.quote: Review the request's details, matched to its type—the time-off window for a time-off request

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing Dynamics 365 and Dataverse security limits WEM tools to the records and actions authorised for the signed-in user.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 and Dataverse security govern access to WEM MCP tools. Tool responses are limited to the records and actions the signed-in user is authorized to access.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The WEM tools require Workforce Engagement Management to be enabled in the environment.
claims.quote: This tool requires the following: Supervisor or reviewer access to Workforce Engagement Management time-off requests. Workforce Engagement Management enabled in the environment.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Listing and opening WEM requests require the signed-in user to have read access.
claims.quote: Workforce Engagement Management must be enabled, and the signed-in user must have read access to WEM requests.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Deciding time-off requests requires supervisor or reviewer access.
claims.quote: Supervisor or reviewer access to Workforce Engagement Management time-off requests.

claims.claim: WEM requests are stored in the Dataverse msdyn_wemrequest table.
claims.quote: Opens the full detail view of a single Dataverse msdyn_wemrequest record.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default of these WEM tools or said that existing behaviour changes.
claims.quote: Searched: WEM MCP tools enabled default administrator configuration; "WEM" "MCP" "default" availability. Read roadmap, WEM overview, all three WEM references, Service Agent FAQ and configuration pages; no WEM-specific arrival default stated.

claims.claim: Service Agent itself requires administrator configuration before use.
claims.quote: Your administrator must configure Service Agent before you can use it.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot is available with Microsoft 365 E7 or as an add-on for eligible commercial, US Government and education plans.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot is available with Microsoft 365 E7 or as an add-on for eligible commercial, US Government, and education subscription plans.

claims.claim: The included licensing model describes a capability within licensed Microsoft Copilot, with tool-specific entitlement explicitly left unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot is available with Microsoft 365 E7 or as an add-on for eligible commercial, US Government, and education subscription plans.

claims.claim: A licence specific to these WEM tools is not yet published.

claims.claim: The roadmap says organisations need not configure a separate permissions framework for these tools.
claims.quote: The integration uses the existing permission model, so organizations don't need to configure a separate permissions framework for these tools

claims.claim: The WEM security roles page and its listed privileges are marked preview.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature. The following tables list each role's privileges in preview.

claims.claim: The dedicated WEM roles page says its roles apply only within the WEM app.
claims.quote: These roles apply only within the Workforce Engagement Management app. They don't replace the Omnichannel supervisor and Omnichannel agent roles or change how those roles work in Copilot Service workspace.

claims.claim: WFM Service Rep is the WEM app role for representatives' own schedules and requests.
claims.quote: WFM Service Rep | Customer service representatives (service representatives or representatives) who view their own schedules and submit their own requests.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The checked documentation does not map the WEM decision tool's reviewer permission to a named security role or privilege.
claims.quote: Searched: "decide_wem_time_off_request" "permission" role confirmation; "Workforce Engagement Management" "reviewer" "privilege". Read decision reference, WEM roles and Customer Service tool privilege reference; no WEM decision-tool mapping listed.

claims.claim: The Workforce Management for Customer Service package must be installed before workforce features can be enabled.
claims.quote: Before you can enable the features to manage your workforce, you must install the Workforce Management for Customer Service package.

claims.claim: Security roles are managed in Power Platform admin center through Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Power Platform admin center. In the site map, select Environments, and then select your environment. Select Settings > Users + permissions > Users. Select the user to update, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.claim: POST /api/data/v9.0/systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<user object ID>)/systemuserroles_association/$ref assigns a security role to a user.
claims.quote:
Assign a security role to a user
POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<user object ID>)/systemuserroles_association/$ref

claims.claim: The Dataverse role-assignment call sets @odata.id in its request body to the role.
claims.quote: { "@odata.id":"[Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/roles(<role ID>)" }

claims.claim: Service app deployment provides an additional app-level access control for the Service Agent experience.
claims.quote: Service app assignment and Microsoft Entra groups | Determines who receives the app and who is allowed to install or use it. Deployment and availability scopes are independent.

claims.claim: Service app availability provides an additional app-level access control.
claims.quote: Available to controls who can install or use the app. These scopes are independent.

claims.claim: Blocking the Service app provides an app-level control over its use.
claims.quote: Blocking prevents installation and use and removes the app from users who already installed it.

claims.claim: Service app deployment, availability and blocking do not target only WEM tools.
claims.quote: Manage deployment at the app level. The package doesn't provide separate administrator targeting for individual Service components. If you remove Service, it can affect more than one experience.

claims.claim: Service Agent supports organisation-level visibility overrides for individual MCP tools.
claims.quote: You can hide tools at the organization level

claims.claim: Service Agent supports profile-level tool visibility overrides.
claims.quote: You can hide tools at the organization level, hide additional tools for a profile

claims.claim: A profile can restore a tool hidden at organisation level.
claims.quote: You can hide tools at the organization level, hide additional tools for a profile, or restore a tool that was hidden at the organization level when working in profile scope.

claims.claim: Learn describes Service Agent tool-availability configuration in maker mode.
claims.quote: You configure these experiences in maker mode, where you can tailor layouts, forms, timelines, tool availability, and default behaviors.

claims.claim: When a name or agent reference matches multiple pending requests, the decision tool lists candidates instead of guessing.
claims.quote: if your reference matches more than one pending request, it lists the matches and asks you to be more specific instead of guessing.
